newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine spring grain sowing complete - AgMin.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine spring grain sowing complete - AgMin.

text.p: Ukraine has finished sowing its spring grain crops and is sticking to a harvest forecast of 35 million tonnes of grain, compared to a poor 25.4 million tonnes in 1996, an Agriculture Ministry official said.
Valentyn Tymoshenko, head of the ministry crops department, said Ukraine has sown 13.51 million hectares to all types of crops, up from last year's 13.12 million hectares.
"Everything is going normally, so we are keeping our previous forecast for this year's grain harvest," Tymoshenko told Reuters.
Private farmers have planted 4.647 million hectares with early spring grain, little changed from year-ago levels, he said.
Volodymyr Krut, deputy head of the Academy of Agrarian Sciences, said recent rains all over the country have given substantial help to crops.
"After a few dry and hot days in the start of the May, we now have good rains and a temperature decrease all over Ukraine," Krut said.
"If we have average weather this summer we would have up to 35 million tonnes of grain," he added.
Krut said most wheat crops were growing in good and satisfactory condition, with a yield potential of about 3.5 tonnes per hectare.

Mykhailo Zubets, deputy prime minister in charge of agriculture and the agriculture minister, said previously Ukraine hoped to harvest 35 million tonnes of grain this year, including 19 million tonnes of wheat.
Last year's drought-ravaged wheat crop stood at 13.5 million tonnes.
Last autumn the country sowed 8.24 million hectares with winter grains, mostly wheat.
It also has sown 1.122 million hectares with maize compared to 869,000 hectares at this time last year.
Last year's maize harvest was 1.8 million tonnes compared to 2.2 million in 1995.
